purpose: Terconazole is used to treat vaginal yeast infections caused by Candida fungus. It helps relieve uncomfortable symptoms like itching, burning, and discharge. It is available as a vaginal cream or suppository that you insert directly into the vagina.
how_it_works: Terconazole works by attacking the outer wall of the yeast cells, which causes them to break down and die. Without that protective wall, the fungus cannot survive or multiply. This clears up the infection and helps your symptoms go away over a few days.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include mild burning, itching, or irritation in the vaginal area after inserting the medication. Some people may feel headaches or have some minor abdominal cramping. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Do not use this medication if you are allergic to terconazole or similar antifungal medicines. Avoid sexual intercourse during treatment, and know that this medication can weaken latex condoms and diaphragms, making them less effective. If you are pregnant, talk to your doctor before using it. See your doctor if your symptoms do not improve within 3 days or do not go away after finishing the full course of treatment.
typical_dosing: The usual treatment is either a 0.4% cream inserted once daily at bedtime for 7 days, a 0.8% cream inserted once daily at bedtime for 3 days, or an 80 mg suppository inserted once daily at bedtime for 3 days. Always finish the full course of treatment even if you start feeling better sooner.
